cultureTransmissionLab.title: How a behavior becomes culture
cultureTransmissionLab.subtitle: One pattern, three explanations — add evidence until only one survives
cultureTransmissionLab.caption: A group difference is only the beginning. Culture becomes the strongest explanation when genes and habitat fail to predict the pattern, while social relationships predict who learns next.

pattern.hint: Difference is a clue, not a verdict.
pattern.aria: Two whale groups showing different behavior with all explanations still possible
pattern.observation: One group performs a behavior that a nearby group does not. That is interesting, but genes, habitat and social learning can all produce the same map.

results.genetic: The groups may carry different inherited tendencies.
results.environmental: One group may encounter a resource or condition the other lacks.
results.social: The behavior may be copied through association. Nothing yet separates the options.

sharedWater.hint: Shared water weakens a purely ecological explanation.
sharedWater.aria: Neighboring whale groups in the same habitat retaining different behaviors
sharedWater.observation: The groups overlap in the same water and can reach the same prey, yet the tradition remains divided along social lines.

results.genetic: Inheritance remains possible until relatedness is measured.
results.environmental: A broad habitat difference no longer explains the social boundary.
results.social: A stable group boundary is what a learned tradition predicts.

geneticOverlap.hint: Genetic overlap removes another easy answer.
geneticOverlap.aria: Genetically overlapping whale groups preserving separate behavior traditions
geneticOverlap.observation: Genetic data do not sort individuals into the same groups as the behavior. Relatives can belong to different traditions; unrelated associates can share one.

results.genetic: Genes no longer predict the behavioral boundary well.
results.environmental: The shared setting has already weakened this alternative.
results.social: Association now predicts the behavior better than ancestry does.

socialDiffusion.hint: The order of adoption follows the social network.
socialDiffusion.aria: A novel behavior spreading from whale to whale along observed social connections
socialDiffusion.observation: A new behavior appears, then reaches close associates before distant individuals. The chronology travels along measured social ties rather than simply across space.

results.genetic: Genes do not change on the timescale of this observed spread.
results.environmental: Nearby non-associates do not acquire the behavior at the same rate.
results.social: The social network predicts who learns next: direct evidence of social transmission.

animalCulture.title: Animal culture
animalCulture.info: A tradition must be learned socially and persist beyond one inventor.
animalCulture.caption: Culture begins with information crossing between lives. Longevity alone is not enough; the route must be social.

socialLearning.title: Social learning
socialLearning.info: Another individual's presence or behavior changes what the observer learns.
socialLearning.caption: Social learning ranges from being drawn to a place another animal uses to copying a novel action with high fidelity.

networkBasedDiffusionAnalysis.title: Network-based diffusion analysis
networkBasedDiffusionAnalysis.info: Tests whether the order of adoption follows measured social ties.
networkBasedDiffusionAnalysis.caption: If close associates reliably acquire a new behavior earlier, a social-transmission model should fit the observed diffusion better than a non-social model.
